title: Finite-stage duality under the site comparison
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$. The finite coefficient stage is $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and let $\nu_X:X_{\mathrm{proet}}\to X_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism].

Use $D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ for the bounded complexes with constructible cohomology [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], and $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ for its full subcategory with Tor amplitude in some finite interval: for some integers $a\le b$ and every degree-zero module sheaf $N$, $\mathcal H^r(K\otimes_A^L N)=0$ for $r\notin[a,b]$ [lem-sf-flat-model]. On the pro-etale site use [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] and [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Internal Hom is the derived sheaf Hom of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on each site.

For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $M\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, the canonical evaluation-defined map
$$
\beta_{K,M}:\nu_X^*R\mathcal Hom_A(K,M)\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_A(\nu_X^*K,\nu_X^*M)
$$
is an isomorphism. Let $a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the structure morphism. Put $\omega_{X,\mathrm{et}}=a_X^{\times}A$, where $a_X^{\times}$ is the etale compact-support right adjoint, and put $\omega_{X,\mathrm{proet}}=Ra_X^!A$, where $Ra_X^!$ is its comparison-class transport [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Then there is a canonical isomorphism
$$
\nu_X^*\omega_{X,\mathrm{et}}\cong\omega_{X,\mathrm{proet}}.
$$
Writing $D_{X,\tau}K=R\mathcal Hom_A(K,\omega_{X,\tau})$ for $\tau=\mathrm{et},\mathrm{proet}$, these comparisons identify the evaluation pairings $D_{X,\tau}K\otimes_A^LK\to\omega_{X,\tau}$ and their transposes $K\to D_{X,\tau}D_{X,\tau}K$ [lem-weil-duality-pairing]. In particular the finite-stage Verdier duality on $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ is transported from etale Verdier duality. No ambient pro-etale exceptional adjoint on arbitrary complexes is assumed.

proof.text: A lisse finite flat sheaf has a degree-zero derived exact pairing, constructed by the proved lisse-flat comparison module. Strong monoidal comparison preserves this pairing, so its canonical internal-Hom comparison is invertible for every target, without a constructibility hypothesis on that target.

For a closed-then-open stratum, construct the ambient closed right adjoints. The proved closed-support comparison identifies their values on bounded-below etale inputs; exact open pullback comparison pastes this to an isomorphism between the two stratum exceptional values. The etale value remains bounded below. This is the coefficient-independent closedComparisonAlpha_isIso argument of lem-weil-finite-duality-closed-comparison, rather than a new arbitrary existence assertion.

Use the two projection-adjunction Hom isomorphisms constructed in lem-sf-stratum-hom-comparison-mate. Compare their middle ordinary direct images using the canonical bounded-below direct-image comparison, the lisse-flat Hom comparison, and the stratum exceptional-value isomorphism. The exact extension comparison identifies the first inputs. This assembles an isomorphism of the two Hom objects on every stratum generator; all component isomorphisms are proved, and no separated-Hom existence theorem is used.

For a strong monoidal left adjoint F, transposing beta through tensor-Hom and F adjunctions gives R(beta) after the unit as Hom(unit) followed by the canonical right-adjoint projection isomorphism. The units are invertible on M and RHom(K,M), since M is bounded below and K bounded above. Therefore R(beta) is invertible. The generator isomorphism of the preceding step puts the target in the essential image of F; both counits are invertible. Counit naturality proves invertibility of the evaluation-defined beta.

Apply the preceding adjunction criterion to each stratum generator. The normalized locally closed sheaf-extension isomorphism identifies the closure generator g_*j_!L with that closed-then-open extension in degree zero. The canonical comparison has a triangulated, retract-stable isomorphism locus, closed under isomorphisms by naturality. Etale thick generation therefore proves invertibility for every constructible finite-Tor K.

The prescribed dualizing arrow is F applied to the etale exceptional functor of the base comparison unit. That unit and its degree-zero constant-unit transport are isomorphisms. Functors preserve isomorphisms, giving exactly the prescribed omega isomorphism.

Canonical exact coefficient realization identifies the intrinsic and fixed-module constructibility predicates and Tor intervals. Bounded constructible origin, bounded-below full faithfulness and preservation/reflection of Tor amplitude yield the equivalence of the two prescribed finite-Tor constructible full subcategories.

The ordinary inverse image is braided by adjunction from sheaf restriction. Derive this braiding equation and conjugate along the canonical derived-functor isomorphism; the prescribed tensor components give the braided structure used by beta. Pairing normalization identifies the recorded evaluation and transpose with native closed-category evaluation and double dual.

Apply evaluation-bidual comparison transport to beta at omega and at the dual of K, the prescribed omega isomorphism and the full-subcategory equivalence. Etale geometric biduality supplies dual preservation and invertible biduality. The transport theorem gives the evaluation square, double-dual square, target anti-equivalence and invertibility of every target bidual map.

proof_origin.place: E9 repair of C-58656: lisse dualizability, proved closed-support comparison, stratum projection-adjunction Hom isomorphisms and bounded-below direct-image comparison; canonicality by the retained monoidal adjunction criterion; thick generation; then the unchanged prescribed dualizing and evaluation-bidual transport assembly.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $X$ be a separated finite-type scheme over
$k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, and let
$\nu_X:X_{\mathrm{proet}}\to X_{\Et}$ be the comparison morphism.
For finite coefficients $A$, $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A)$, and
$M\in D^b_c(X_{\Et},A)$, the canonical map

$$
\nu_X^*R\mathcal Hom_A(K,M)
\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_A(\nu_X^*K,\nu_X^*M)
$$

is an isomorphism. Moreover
$\nu_X^*\omega_{X,\Et}\cong\omega_{X,\mathrm{proet}}$, and these
comparisons identify evaluations and double-dual maps. In particular
finite-stage Verdier duality on the pro-etale constructible category
is transported from etale Verdier duality.

proof.text:
The comparison for $Rj_*$, including a quasi-compact open immersion
$j$, is [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image]. The exact
comparison pullback commutes with the open restrictions and closed
direct images, as their stalk and extension-by-zero descriptions show.
Apply it to the closed-support triangle of
[lem-exc-closed-support-triangle]; the first comparison identifies
the third term with the pro-etale $Rj_*j^*$ term. Full faithfulness
of closed direct image then gives
$\nu_Z^*Ri_{\Et}^!M\cong Ri_{\mathrm{proet}}^!\nu_X^*M$.
This establishes the required closed exceptional comparison directly
from recollement, without an assertion that closed ordinary restriction
commutes with internal Hom.

The finite stratification in
[lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata], and the triangles of
[def-weil-open-closed-recollement], reduce internal-Hom comparison
to $K=Rs_!P$, with $P$ site-perfect: internal Hom is triangulated in
the first variable by [lem-sf-hom-triangulated] (the same Hom-complex
argument applies on the pro-etale site), and the exact $\nu^*$ carries
triangles to triangles, so the comparison maps form morphisms of
triangles. On both sites the identity
of [lem-weil-stratum-ambient-hom] reads

$$
R\mathcal Hom(Rs_!P,M)
=Rs_*R\mathcal Hom(P,Rs^!M).
$$

The locally closed $Rs^!$ commutes with $\nu^*$ by the open and
closed comparisons above. The site-perfect complex $P$ of
[def-weil-site-perfect-complex] is locally a bounded complex of finite
free modules, and for such a first variable and a bounded constructible
second variable the internal Hom commutes with $\nu^*$ by
[lem-sf-hom-comparison-finite-free]; the question being local, this
applies to $R\mathcal Hom(P,Rs^!M)$. Finally $Rs_*$ commutes with comparison by
[prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image]. Hence the specified
internal-Hom map is an isomorphism on every stratum generator and then
on $K$.

Locally embed $X$ as a closed subscheme of a smooth affine space.
On both sites its dualizing object is the closed exceptional inverse
image of the smooth dualizing object. Smooth purity
[thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity] and the closed comparison
just proved identify these objects; uniqueness of the adjunction
comparisons makes the local identifications agree on overlaps.
The Hom comparisons are defined by evaluation, so they identify its
transpose, the double-dual map, as well. Finally the equivalence of
bounded constructible categories is
[lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], and finite Tor intervals
are preserved and detected by [lem-exc-comparison-tor-interval].
